newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: FOCUS - San Miguel sees global growth from CC-Amatil deal.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - San Miguel sees global growth from CC-Amatil deal.

text.p: Food and beverage firm San Miguel Corp plans to merge its bottling unit with Australia's Coca-Cola Amatil Ltd, a move that will bring it global growth opportunities, San Miguel said on Thursday.

Already a player in China and elsewhere abroad with its beer-making operations, the merger of San Miguel's majority-owned Coca-Cola Bottlers Philippines Inc with Coca-Cola Co affiliate C-C Amatil dramatically diversifies its soft drinks interests.

"In one dynamic step, we shall have expanded the horizon of our soft-drink business from the domestic market servicing 68 million consumers to an international arena spanning three continents with a consumer base of 448 million," Francisco Eizmendi, the firm's president and chief operating officer, told a news conference.
Delfin Gonzalez, San Miguel's chief finance officer, said the transaction would "result in a small amount (of net income) this year and growing in the next few years". He declined to give specifics.
The merger of the companies, which would involve the issue of 293 million shares by C-C Amatil worth about $2.7 billion, will create the biggest Coca-Cola bottling group outside the United States.
The combined sales revenue of C-C Amatil and Coca-Cola Bottlers in 1996 amounted to $3.7 billion and operating income of $438 million, San Miguel said.
San Miguel will be the merged company's second biggest stockholder with a 25 percent stake, with Coca-Cola retaining majority ownership at 33 percent.
Although San Miguel will be giving up control of its bottling firm because of the merger, it will have a larger market share as a result of the deal.

Coca-Cola Bottling has 75 percent of the soft drinks market in the Philippines and contributed to 39 percent of San Miguel's net income in 1996. The firm posted 6.09 billion pesos ($231.56 million) in net income last year, including one-time gains.

"It will mean better revenues for San Miguel, which is also expanding its beer operations abroad. It will indeed expose San Miguel to larger markets aside from the Philippines," said Alexis Cabe, analyst at Angping & Associates Securities.
Indeed, San Miguel's officials said it hoped to participate in Coca-Cola franchises.
Eizmendi said: "We have the potential to be offered other franchises (of Coke) as they become available." He cited India as a possible new market.
"Coke recently re-entered India and may be looking for partners. We foresee at some point they will be able to offer the franchise," Eizmendi said.
Amid a sharply weaker Manila stock market, San Miguel's A stock closed unchanged at 55 pesos, while its more indicative B stock ended off 1.50 pesos to 90 after rising to as high as 92 pesos.
But Eizmendi said the merger could lead to more attractive values for the company's share price.
"Since CCA is a listed company, the transaction will allow analysts to put a public market value on San Miguel's soft drink investment," he said.
He said that Coca-Cola anchor bottlers -- those that bottle for their own and other markets -- tended to trade at price-earnings multiples "higher than food and beverage companies".
